common_name: Judge Solomon Azalea (Bright Orange-Red Southern Indica)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5-6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade; Judge Solomon was bred in Mobile, Alabama and remains a Deep South landscape standard for its bright, saturated bloom color.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5-6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade with protection from hot afternoon sun. Judge Solomon is a classic Southern Indica azalea bred in Mobile, Alabama, one of the historic centers of azalea breeding in the Deep South, and is prized for its vivid orange-red flowers produced in an overwhelming spring flush on a large, vigorous, evergreen shrub. It has been a fixture of historic Gulf Coast azalea gardens and estate plantings for generations, valued for the sheer volume and intensity of its bloom. Water deeply during dry spells, especially while establishing, and prune lightly right after flowering if shaping is needed, since flower buds for the following year set soon after bloom ends.
sources: University of Georgia Cooperative Extension — Azalea Cultivars for the Landscape
American Rhododendron Society
Texas A&M AgriLife Extension — Azaleas for Texas Gardens

common_name: Mrs. G.G. Gerbing Azalea (Pure White Southern Indica)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5-6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade; Mrs. G.G. Gerbing is a white-flowered sport of George Tabor and one of the most widely planted white azaleas in Deep South gardens.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5-6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade, giving the large mature shrub room to spread. Mrs. G.G. Gerbing arose as a pure white sport of the pink Southern Indica azalea George Tabor and has itself become one of the most planted white azaleas across the Deep South, producing an overwhelming spring flush of large, pure white flowers on a big, vigorous evergreen shrub. Its size and heavy bloom make it a favorite for estate plantings, historic gardens, and hedges where a dramatic white spring display is wanted. Water deeply during establishment and dry spells, and prune only right after flowering if needed, since next year's buds form soon after bloom ends.

Texas A&M AgriLife Extension — Azaleas for Texas Gardens

common_name: Pride of Mobile Azalea (Deep Watermelon-Pink Southern Indica)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5-6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade; Pride of Mobile is a classic Southern Indica azalea named for the historic Mobile, Alabama azalea trail gardens.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5-6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade with room for the shrub to reach full size. Pride of Mobile is a historic Southern Indica azalea associated with the famed azalea trail gardens of Mobile, Alabama, prized for its deep, saturated watermelon-pink flowers produced in a spectacular spring flush on a large, vigorous evergreen shrub. Like other Southern Indica cultivars it has proven itself over generations of Gulf Coast gardens for reliability, size, and sheer bloom impact, making it a striking specimen or hedge plant in large landscapes. Water deeply during establishment and dry periods, and prune lightly right after flowering if shaping is needed, since flower buds for next spring set soon after bloom ends.

common_name: Duc de Rohan Azalea (Antique Salmon-Orange Southern Indica)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5-6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade; Duc de Rohan is an antique Southern Indica azalea long grown in old Gulf South gardens for its warm salmon-orange bloom color.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5-6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade, allowing plenty of room for the mature shrub's spread. Duc de Rohan is an antique Southern Indica azalea cultivar that has been grown in old Gulf South gardens for generations, valued for its warm, unusual salmon-orange flowers that stand apart from the more common pinks, reds, and whites of other Southern Indica cultivars. The large, evergreen shrub produces its heaviest bloom in a single dramatic spring flush and provides dense structural greenery the rest of the year. Water deeply while establishing and during dry spells, and prune only right after flowering if shaping is needed, since flower buds for the following spring form soon after bloom ends.

common_name: Fielder's White Azalea (Heavy-Blooming Pure White Southern Indica)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5-6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade; Fielder's White is a classic Southern Indica azalea grown across the Deep South for its exceptionally heavy pure white spring bloom.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5-6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade, giving the large mature shrub adequate room to spread. Fielder's White is a Southern Indica azalea long favored in Deep South gardens for the sheer density of its pure white spring flowers, which can cover the entire shrub so thoroughly that little foliage shows through during peak bloom. Its large, vigorous, evergreen habit makes it well suited to hedges, screens, and estate-scale plantings where a dramatic white spring display is wanted. Water deeply during establishment and dry spells, and prune lightly right after flowering if shaping is needed, since flower buds for next year's bloom set soon after the spring flush ends.

common_name: President Clay Azalea (Classic Salmon-Orange Southern Indica)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5-6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade; President Clay is a classic Southern Indica azalea long grown in historic Gulf South gardens for its warm salmon-orange bloom color.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5-6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade, allowing plenty of room for the shrub's mature spread. President Clay is a historic Southern Indica azalea cultivar bearing warm salmon-orange flowers in a heavy spring flush, one of the classic color selections that have anchored Deep South azalea gardens and public azalea trails for generations. The large, vigorous evergreen shrub provides dense year-round structure and a spectacular seasonal display, making it a strong choice for large borders, screens, and historic garden restorations. Water deeply while establishing and during dry periods, and prune only right after flowering if shaping is needed, since next year's flower buds form soon after bloom ends.

common_name: Christmas Cheer Azalea (Very Early-Blooming Red Kurume Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5-6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade; Christmas Cheer is one of the earliest-blooming landscape azaleas, often flowering well before most other Kurume and Southern Indica cultivars.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5-6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade with good air circulation. Christmas Cheer is a compact Kurume-type azalea grown widely in Southern landscapes for its unusually early spring bloom, often opening its bright red to red-pink, hose-in-hose flowers well ahead of most other azalea cultivars and giving an early jolt of color to the late-winter garden. Its dense, mounding, evergreen habit suits foundation plantings, borders, and mass plantings where reliable early color is wanted. Water deeply during dry spells, especially while establishing, and prune lightly right after flowering if shaping is needed, since flower buds for next year's bloom set soon after the spring flush ends.
